title: Terraform registry publish & breaking-change playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose & scope:
This is a working playbook for publishing Terraform modules used by Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, managing semantic versioning, and coordinating breaking changes. Intended for eng-private-deployments + platform eng owners. Draft notes, checklist items, and rollout templates here — keep rough.

Audience:
- Module authors and reviewers
- Release engineers who push registry tags and create module releases
- Solutions / SEs who coordinate customer upgrades for Private deployments

Assumptions:
- We publish modules to our private Terraform registry (Terraform Cloud or GitHub registry), and also mirror tags in the terraform-modules monorepo.
- Consumers pin module versions in their root Terraform (module
      source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//modules/foo?ref=v1.2.0"
) or via registry name.
- State is managed per-customer for Private deployments; upgrades must be safe for state migrations.

Quick rules (TL;DR):
- Follow SemVer: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
  - PATCH: bugfix, no behavior change.
  - MINOR: new optional resources/parameters, backwards compatible.
  - MAJOR: incompatible changes (resource renames, param reshapes, provider upgrades that change semantics).
- Tag releases and create release notes before publishing.
- Any MAJOR bump requires a documented migration plan, a canary upgrade, and an approved rollback.

Module versioning details:
- Version file: keep a top-level RELEASE_VERSION in the module folder for easy grepping (optional but recommended).
- Changelog: maintain CHANGELOG.md in the module dir. Use conventional commits for PR messages to auto-generate a draft changelog.
- Branching model:
  - All changes land on main via PRs.
  - For a release, create release branch release/vX.Y.0 if multiple PRs/updates are grouped.
  - Tag from release branch.

Registry publishing procedure (manual flow):
1) Finalize release PR(s): ensure acceptance tests pass (unit tests, terraform init/plan with example configs). Link all dependent PRs.
2) Update CHANGELOG.md and bump RELEASE_VERSION.
3) Create release branch if needed: git checkout -b release/vX.Y.Z
4) Create annotated tag: git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m vX.Y.Z
5) Push branch and tags: git push origin release/vX.Y.Z && git push --tags
6) Create GitHub release or push to Terraform Cloud private registry (depending on our registry). Confirm module is visible in registry and that source module reference resolves.
7) Post-publish smoke tests:
   - terraform init against the registry in a clean workspace.
   - terraform plan using pinned vX.Y.Z in a test account/operator workspace.
   - run module examples / integration harness (see linked artifacts).
8) Update docs and release notes (confluence + docs repo).
9) Notify customers and internal stakeholders via #private-deployments Slack channel and create a release Jira ticket.

Checklist for non-breaking (PATCH/MINOR) releases:
- [ ] PR includes tests and example updates.
- [ ] CHANGELOG updated with user-facing notes.
- [ ] Module output/inputs compatibility assertion added in PR description.
- [ ] Automated tests pass across supported terraform/provider versions (matrix).
- [ ] Release notes published.

Breaking-change (MAJOR) checklist (must be green before merging):
- [ ] Design doc in Confluence describing the change, motivation, and migration strategy (link in PR).
- [ ] A state migration plan is drafted and reviewed by SRE and platform eng. Includes terraform state mv commands, resource replacement plan, and expected downtime.
- [ ] E2E upgrade runbook for Private deployment customers, including: backup step, pre-check list, canary cohort instructions, and rollback steps.
- [ ] Small-scale canary tested in an internal staging customer instance.
- [ ] Customer impact matrix: list of customers using the module + estimated effort to upgrade.
- [ ] Communication plan: customer notices, scheduled maintenance windows, and SE hand-holding tasks.
- [ ] Tag the module MAJOR version and mark older minor/patch versions as supported for a defined window (e.g., 90 days).
- [ ] Post-upgrade validation assertions to run after canary and full rollout.

State migration patterns and examples:
- When renaming resources (avoid if possible):
  - Plan: introduce new resource with new name as optional, create mapping, then run terraform state mv from old to new in a maintenance window.
  - Example: terraform state mv module.foo.aws_instance.old_name module.foo.aws_instance.new_name
  - Note: always run a plan after state mv and take a snapshot of state file (or backup backend snapshot).
- When changing a parameter from single value to list/map: add a compatibility layer (accept old param and coerce into the new shape) for at least one MINOR cycle, then deprecate.

Upgrade plan template (for a single customer/private cluster):
1) Pre-upgrade:
   - Snapshot state backend (manual snapshot or cloud snapshot).
   - Run terraform plan against current pinned version and assert no diffs.
   - Create a customer-specific canary workspace (or pick one low-risk customer).
2) Canary upgrade:
   - Apply module vX.Y.Z to canary workspace with maintenance window.
   - Run integration smoke tests and app-level checks.
   - If any issue: immediately revert by re-applying previous pinned module version and open incident.
3) Gradual rollout:
   - Batch customers into waves (size depends on risk).
   - For each wave: apply, run smoke tests, validate logs and metrics, wait 24-72 hours.
4) Full rollout:
   - Apply to remaining customers during scheduled windows.
5) Post-upgrade:
   - Run post-check automation; close Jira when all waves pass.

Rollback playbook (fast):
- If an apply fails or post-checks show regressions:
  1) Pause rollout.
  2) Re-apply previous module version in the failed workspace.
  3) If state was migrated, follow documented reverse migration steps (capture evidential logs).
  4) Communicate to stakeholders and open follow-up bug PRs.

Testing matrix suggestions (automate in CI):
- TF core versions: 1.5.x, 1.6.x (example)
- Provider versions: aws ~> 4.x, random other providers used.
- Example modules: one minimal, one full stack (VPC + SG + instances + LB).
- Run: terraform init, terraform validate, terraform plan (expect no diffs on pinned test fixture), and a local apply/destroy in ephemeral env.

Release notes outline:
- Summary (1-2 lines)
- Notable changes (breaking changes called out up front)
- Upgrade notes (explicit commands for state moves)
- Tests & verification steps
- Contact & rollback instructions

PR checklist for authors (quick):
- [ ] Add CHANGELOG entry
- [ ] Add tests or update examples
- [ ] Link design doc / migration plan for breaking changes
- [ ] Add compatibility matrix entry if providers/TF versions change
- [ ] Tag reviewers: module owners + SRE + platform eng

Notifications & tracking:
- Create a Jira for the release (include release link, customer list, roll-out schedule).
- Post in #private-deployments with TL;DR and link to Confluence runbook.
- For MAJOR: Ops on call should be paged during canary window; add documented runbook steps.

Notes-to-self / open questions (TODOs):
- Decide canonical registry: Terraform Cloud private registry vs GitHub modules registry for mirror. Pros/cons: Terraform Cloud has nice UI for versions, GH registry mirrors work well with our CI.
- Do we want automated semantic-release pipeline that tags & publishes for non-breaking changes? Might be risky for Private customers — prefer manual approval.
- Need a standardized example suite per module that can run in CI using ephemeral cloud accounts (cost + cleanup considerations).
- Investigate a preflight tool that detects potentially breaking provider upgrades (provider diffing).

References and useful commands (examples):
- Tag & push: git tag -a v1.3.0 -m v1.3.0 && git push origin --tags
- Publish: create GitHub release or use terraform cloud registry UI / API to publish module source
- Test plan: terraform init && terraform plan -out tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan > plan.json
- State move example: terraform state mv module.foo.aws_elb.old module.foo.aws_elb.new

End of draft. Keep this file as the working master list of steps and change it as we discover better automation or patterns.

Unresolved (explicit):
- What is the support window policy for older minor versions after a major? propose 90 days but needs legal/CS signoff.
- Template for customer-facing upgrade communication (SaaS vs Private) — draft an email template and SE checklist.

Authors: Priya (owner), Marcus, Sofia, Ben.
